key_insight: Decouple reasoning (understanding) from image generation by using a dedicated image-editing model guided by the model's intermediate reasoning, so that targeted, iterative edits clarify visual context and produce cleaner, more useful visual chain-of-thoughts.
problem_solved: Addresses limitations of textual-only chains of thought and noisy or inflexible 'think with images' methods by providing a modular way to generate clear, interpretable intermediate images that support fine-grained focus and view transformations.
method: Separate modules: a multimodal understanding/ reasoning mode produces explicit editing instructions, and a specialized image-editing model executes targeted visual changes.
Iterative edit-and-reason loop: produce intermediate reasoning steps, translate them into concrete edits (focus, crop, viewpoint, annotations), apply edits, and re-evaluate to refine answers.
Modularity enables controllability and reduced noise versus unified multimodal generators; editing is constrained to purposeful transformations rather than free-form image synthesis.
impact: Enables more reliable, interpretable visual reasoning by producing purposeful intermediate images that improve accuracy and user trust; the modular design eases integration, debugging, and component upgrades for ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing decoupled 'Understanding/Reasoning' module feeding edit instructions to an 'Image Editing' module and looping back for refinement.
Before/after example pair(s) of images illustrating targeted edits (e.g., crop, highlight, viewpoint change) plus the corresponding reasoning step.
A short stepwise reasoning trace combining text steps and the edited images as a visual chain-of-thought.
Bar chart comparing task accuracy and image-noise/clarity metrics against fixed-toolkit and unified multimodal baselines.
paper_title: ETCHR: Editing To Clarify and Harness Reasoning
paper_authors: Beichen Zhang, Yuhong Liu, Jinsong Li, Yuhang Zang, Jiaqi Wang
